subject: Workload sizing & guaranteed throughput — Dedicated commit options
messages:
From: Evan Liu <evan@novusai.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sophie Tran <sophie@novusai.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick ask — expected QPS, context length, and committed discount bands

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — the throughput numbers looked promising. Before we lock capacity with Procurement, Sophie and I need a concise sizing recommendation we can take to Finance: expected sustained QPS for our baseline and peak, recommended GPU pool (count + model mix), and the pricing tiers (3-, 6-, 12-month commits) with any discount thresholds.

We currently expect:~
- Traffic: 45 requests/sec baseline, 120 req/sec peak (short bursts)
- Typical context length: 1.5k tokens average, 6k tokens max for long-form generation
- Concurrency target: ~30 simultaneous active sessions during peaks

Attached is a CSV export of our usage patterns (novus_workload_profile_20261015.csv). Appreciate a short proposal we can share internally — focus on throughput guarantees and the delta to support 6k token flows.

Best,
Evan
CTO, Novus AI
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Liu <evan@novusai.com>
Cc: Sophie Tran <sophie@novusai.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick ask — expected QPS, context length, and committed discount bands

Evan — thanks for the data and clear ask. I ran a quick back-of-envelope model and pulled our throughput curves; outlining the short answer below and attaching a detailed proposal (redwood_proposal_v3.pdf) and a sizing worksheet.

Summary recommendation (short):
- Baseline (45 QPS): 4 x A100-class GPU workers in a dedicated pool with auto-burst to 6 for short peaks.
- Peak target (120 QPS, 6k context): 8 x A100-class GPU workers (or 10 x T4-equivalent if using smaller models) to keep tail latency < 300 ms for generation-heavy flows.
- Commit options: 3-month commit: 10% discount off list; 6-month: 18%; 12-month: 28% — we can structure a fast-path pilot (90 days) with credits applied toward a longer commit if you convert.

Notes:
- The 6k token path is the cost driver: long context increases KV cache memory and per-token compute. For mixed workloads we recommend a model mix: 70% short-context optimized (2–2.5k token quantized variant) + 30% long-context (6k capable) and route by policy.
- We provision burst capacity to guarantee latency SLOs; bursts are billed at a higher transient rate unless covered by a bursting add-on in the reserved plan.

I'll loop in Marissa and Ben for pricing/legal details — they will draft explicit committed pricing and SLA language. Do you have a target budget range so we can refine the discounting band?

—Kimberly
Sr. Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_proposal_v3.pdf (proposal), sizing_sheet.xlsx (workload worksheet)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-18T13:27:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Novus AI sizing request — ask for pricing + pool recommendation

Team — forwarding Novus AI's profile. Evan provided baseline and peak QPS and long-context requirements. Key asks: recommended pool size, commit length discounts, and a throughput SLA we can promise for their Finance/Procurement review.

Core constraints:
- Baseline 45 QPS, peak bursts to 120 QPS (short windows), average context 1.5k, max 6k.
- They want explicit pricing for 3/6/12 month commits and any conversion credits if they pilot.

My quick take (from the proposal): 4 workers baseline, 8 workers for guaranteed peak; recommend commit pricing tied to sustained baseline with a burst buffer. Please draft two pricing structures:
A) Conservative: commit to baseline (45 QPS) with burst add-on; 3/6/12 month discounts (10/18/28).
B) Aggressive: commit to 75 QPS sustained (covers most peaks) with smaller burst and higher discount at 12 months.

Ben — can you run numbers for both structures (unit $/GPU-hour, monthly commit fee, token pricing delta for long-context flows)? Priyom — can you draft SLA text for throughput and latency with canary fallback to hosted variants? Marissa — legal & credits language (pilot -> commit).

Thanks — need a draft we can send Evan by EOD tomorrow.

—Kimberly
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-19T11:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Novus AI sizing request — ask for pricing + pool recommendation

All — ran the two structures in the cost model (attached sizing outputs in sizing_sheet.xlsx). High-levels:
- Conservative (commit-to-baseline 45 QPS)
  - Pool: 4 x A100 (baseline active), burst to 6 for 15% of traffic (billing at burst rate when used).
  - Monthly commit fee: $96,000 (includes baseline compute + KV cache reservation).
  - Long-context delta: +24% token compute premium for 6k flows (we account for memory pressure and longer token decode).
- Aggressive (commit-to-75 QPS sustained)
  - Pool: 6 x A100 baseline, burst to 9 for headroom.
  - Monthly commit fee: $156,000.
  - Long-context delta: +18% token compute premium (improved utilization spreads KV overhead).

Discount stitching suggestions:
- 3-month: baseline discount off list (10%); 6-month: 16% (we can slightly sweeten); 12-month: 30% (need SOC/contract sign-off).
- Pilot conversion credit: apply up to 40% of pilot charges as a one-time credit on first invoice when converting to a 12-month commit.

I've included assumptions in the sheet (token mix, 2.5x cost multiplier for burst hours). If they share target spend or preferred commit length, we can tune.

—Ben
VP, Solutions Pricing

Attachment: sizing_sheet.xlsx (detailed model outputs)
From: Evan Liu <evan@novusai.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Sophie Tran <sophie@novusai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-22T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Workload sizing & guaranteed throughput — Dedicated commit options

Kimberly / team — thanks, this is very helpful. A few quick clarifications before we present to Finance Monday:
1) If we pick the Aggressive plan (6 x A100 baseline) and convert after a 90-day pilot, do you guarantee the 75 QPS sustained SLO? What are remediation/credits if we miss SLO during steady state (not pilot)?
2) The long-context premium is expected — can you confirm whether token pricing is flat or we bill additional "context tax" only when >4k tokens?
3) Can you put the pilot conversion credit terms into the proposal PDF (redwood_proposal_v3.pdf) and include a sample SLA clause for throughput credits?

We're leaning toward the Aggressive commit if you can back the SLO and structure the pilot conversion credit. Target: sign a 12-month commitment in November if pilot looks good.

Thanks,
Evan
CTO, Novus AI
